Axiom: Exception handling is mandatory in business logic. Any business method with network/file/process I/O, mutation of external state, or integration with an external system MUST wrap the failure point in `try`/`catch` per `AX_CATCH_LOG_RECOVER`. Missing try/catch on an integration boundary turns any transient failure into an un-traced un-contextualized exception. This is strictest at a PUBLIC API boundary: canon is throw a typed `Error` subclass (`AX_ERROR_VIA_CLASS`) from the failure point, mandatory try/catch at the boundary that calls it — not a `Result` return threaded through the call chain (`AX_RESULT_PUBLIC_BOUNDARY` — Result stays a narrow, contract-scoped exception, never the default error-handling mechanism for new public surfaces).
